cases.input: Evaluate licensing a biosensor platform for three IVD reference applications: T1D autoantibodies, anti-nephrin autoantibodies and blood pTau217. Technical documents, pilot data, commercial assumptions and public patent evidence are available.
requiredBehaviors: classify each specialist domain through the routing gate before invoking or reusing specialist work
coordinate required offer patent FTO regulatory and supplier outputs rather than reproducing their analyses
produce decision drivers red flags preconditions a decision posture and one next safe action across the three application scenarios
forbiddenBehaviors: create independent claim charts regulatory classifications or supplier approvals inside the orchestrator
invent a composite score without confirmed weighting

cases.input: The technology evidence is strong, but the FTO specialist reports a high-priority technical concern and unresolved items while intended-use and regulatory-performance assumptions are still unstable before a licensing decision.
requiredBehaviors: prevent a blanket supportable decision posture despite strong technical evidence
surface FTO counsel and regulatory preconditions as blockers or bounded investigations
preserve specialist uncertainty without translating it into an invented score
forbiddenBehaviors: average FTO and regulatory unknowns into a reassuring overall score
silently convert specialist uncertainty into a positive assumption
skillAnchors: Kritische Unknowns nicht in Scores verstecken

cases.input: A draft executive DD invents its own claim charts, chooses an IVDR classification, declares the supplier qualified and summarizes all domains as 82 out of 100 despite unresolved FTO and regulatory gaps.
requiredBehaviors: reject duplicated specialist analysis and the invented composite score
mark required missing specialist assessments as blocked or evidence-insufficient and create bounded next investigations only where needed
forbiddenBehaviors: simulate legal regulatory supplier or board authority
hide unresolved domain blockers behind a numerical roll-up
skillAnchors: keine eigene Patent-, Claim-, Regulatory- oder Supplier-Quality-Fachlogik

cases.input: Compare two early preclinical sensing platforms for research scouting. No product architecture, target commercialization date or fixed market jurisdiction exists yet.
requiredBehaviors: classify technology assessment as required while full FTO is normally not required or optional at this stage
avoid forcing a claim-by-claim FTO assessment without a stable product baseline
document why deferred domains are not required for the current decision
forbiddenBehaviors: automatically trigger full FTO merely because patents may exist
manufacture a target jurisdiction solely to satisfy the workflow

cases.input: The target has a current counsel-provided patent/FTO memo, a current regulatory specialist assessment and a completed supplier-quality assessment. The user asks for executive technology due diligence synthesis.
requiredBehaviors: classify the supplied specialist domains as already available
consume and cite the existing specialist outputs instead of rerunning them
limit new analysis to missing cross-domain synthesis and decision-relevant gaps
forbiddenBehaviors: rerun patent FTO regulatory or supplier analysis simply because the orchestrator can route to those skills
overwrite specialist uncertainty with a new orchestrator judgment

cases.input: A small make/buy DD has complete technical and commercial evidence, no material regulatory or IP trigger, and no blocking investigation. A concise executive synthesis is requested.
requiredBehaviors: complete the due diligence without invoking large-work-wayfinder
mark non-applicable domains explicitly and produce the decision posture and next safe action directly
forbiddenBehaviors: invoke wayfinder merely because it is available
create artificial investigations to satisfy a workflow template
